claim: Skype 8.0 for desktop released July 17, 2018, with free HD video/screensharing calls, @mentions, chat media gallery, drag-and-drop file sharing up to 300MB.
At the July 2018 8.0 launch Microsoft said upcoming planned features included read receipts, private conversations, cloud-based call recording, and profile invites/group links.
Microsoft set September 1, 2018 as the date after which only Skype 8.0 would function, discontinuing Skype 7.0.
Microsoft released the first version of Skype 8 (preview) to the public in October 2017.
Skype 8.61 (desktop) and Skype for Windows 10 v15 (Store), both Electron-based, released June 24, 2020.
The move to Electron removed People app integration, Outlook sync, automatic Microsoft Account sign-in, process throttling, and Windows share context menu.
Microsoft explained the Electron migration would allow developers to adapt Skype for more platforms, such as Chrome OS.
8.61/v15 added bulk contact deletion, 9-video call support, background replacement, Android Auto compatibility.
Microsoft announced Feb 28, 2025 that Skype would remain available until May 5, 2025.
Skype subscription users could continue using Skype Credits/subscriptions until end of next renewal period.
Users could migrate to Teams via sign-in (auto chats/contacts) or export data (chats, contacts, call history).
Teams users can call and chat with Skype users during transition.
Skype officially retired May 5, 2025; website now redirects to Teams.
After retirement, existing Skype Credit for outgoing calls usable via Skype Dial Pad web app, no new credit purchasable.
In April 2017 Microsoft moved Skype from peer-to-peer to central server based system.
The 2017 Skype redesign was not well-received, with negative reviews/complaints of broken functionality.
Skype 8 desktop (2018) supports HD (1080p) video calls up to 24 people, and screen-sharing in calls.
Skype 8.0 desktop added a chat media gallery.
Skype 8.0 desktop added support for @mentions in chats.
Skype 8.0 desktop allows file and media sharing up to 300 MB.
Microsoft announced planned built-in call recording where everyone in call is notified, recordings capture video/screen shares.
E2E encrypted chat (Signal Protocol) announced coming to Skype 8, notifications hidden in chat list.
Skype Store (UWP) app has Settings menu with General, Messaging, Help & Feedback categories.
Desktop (Win32) Skype 8 variant has options UWP lacks: auto-start, tray persistence, Cortana suggestions, chat history export, text size, DirectShow camera inputs.
Skype UWP and desktop apps 'look the same' because 'They're both based on Skype 8.'
Skype 2018 desktop redesign gave multi-colored group chats and bright squiggly lines for typing/unread indicators.
Skype's 'Highlights' feature (Snapchat/Stories-style) let users snap photo/video, decorate, post for followers.
Skype rolled back parts of redesign in Sept 2018, ditching Stories/Highlights, squiggle indicators, over-the-top color.
Skype 8's redesign was 'much-debated' before reaching desktop.
Microsoft added dark mode (v8.52, ~Sept 2019) with two dark variants and 'Use system setting' option.
Skype 8.x on Windows can hide menu bar by default; Alt reveals it temporarily.
'Online' status set automatically by default; friends can contact any way; sender gets immediate notification.
'Offline' status shown automatically when Skype closed or chosen manually; cannot receive calls/IMs.
'Away' status means user left computer; can still be messaged/called, sound alerts if nearby.
'Do Not Disturb' status: online but notifications arrive without sound, only subtle taskbar badge.
'Invisible' status shares icon with Offline; user still receives notifications of messages/calls.
'Blocked' status: blacklisted users see owner as Offline, no notifications until unblocked, then old messages delivered.
'Unauthorized' status appears for users not in contact list; calls/messages go through only if privacy settings allow anyone.
'Away' auto-trigger configurable via Tools/Settings > General > inactivity minutes setting, disable by unchecking or 0.
Group chat commands work only in group chats, split by P2P/cloud type; not all supported in all Skype versions.
/add username(s) adds specified Skype users to chat, supported P2P and cloud.
/kick removes user (can rejoin); /kickban removes and revokes right to return.
/setrole sets chat member role; roles include admin/master/helper/listener via /get admins/masters/helpers/listeners.
/createmoderatedchat creates moderated group chat, equivalent to /newchat + /set options +MODERATED.
/set allowlist and /set banlist manage join permissions using +/- prefixes.
/get uri creates unique invite URL for group chat.
/golive starts group call involving all users in chat.
/history loads entire correspondence history of active chat window.
Cloud chats named '19:***@thread.skype'; P2P chats named '#username$***'.
Typing indicator disabled via Tools > Options > IM & SMS > IM Settings > Show Advanced Options, untick 'Show when I am typing'.
Edit/delete message via right-click 'Edit Message'/'Remove Message'; recipient sees indicator, not content.
Skype's Expression Picker offers emojis, GIFs, stickers, Mojis.
Skype has hidden emoticons not shown in regular menu, some requiring specific text codes.
Skype 8.0 desktop supports HD (1080p) video calls up to 24 people.
Skype 8.0 supports screen-sharing in calls.
Skype 8.0 added built-in cloud call recording; everyone notified.
Cloud call recordings additionally include everyone's video and screen shares.
Skype 8.0 supports file and media sharing up to 300 MB.
Skype 8.0 introduced @mentions in group chats and chat media gallery.
In 2019 Skype added AI-based software-only background blur, no depth camera needed.
On April 5, 2019, Skype doubled group call participant limit from 25 to 50.
With 2019 expansion, Skype changed default group-call notification sound to ping instead of ring, kept old ring for <25 participants; users can individually ring specific participants.
The 50-participant limit rollout was tested with Skype Insider Preview beta users in March 2019 before public rollout in April 2019.
Skype desktop has Notifications settings tab (triple-dot menu > Settings > Notifications) with 'Contact comes online notification' toggle.
Skype users can call landline/mobile numbers (formerly SkypeOut) via Skype Credit/subscription, and purchase Skype Number (formerly SkypeIn) for inbound calls.
Group video calling and screen sharing (previously Premium, screen share limited to 10 people) made free in summer 2014 when Premium removed; baseline carried into 8.x.
